title: arXiv Mathematics — daily notable papers, 20 October 2026
global_caveat: This is an editorial shortlist, not an official arXiv trending chart or measured popularity ranking; citation and independent-attention evidence for same-day submissions is limited, and the preprint claims have not been independently verified.

sections.title: Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Erdős-Szemerédi conjecture: for every fixed number of petals k≥3, a family of subsets of [n] containing no k-sunflower has size at most c_k^n for some c_k<2.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 states an exponentially improved upper bound below 2^n for sunflower-free set families for each k≥3; the full text reduces to a vector sunflower bound proved with a polynomial-method dimension argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed integer k≥3 and n-element ground set; the family contains no k sets whose pairwise intersections all coincide.
sections.unique_caveat: The newly posted preprint's proof has not been independently checked here; the paper discusses lower bounds that leave room to investigate the sharp exponential base.

sections.title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet L-functions
sections.abstract: The paper proves unconditional positive proportions of isolated Riemann-zeta zeros and moderate consecutive gaps, then applies an unconditional refinement of the Bombieri–Hejhal method to improve a lower bound for critical-line zeros of certain two-term Dirichlet L-function combinations.
sections.claimed_result: The paper gives a limiting lower proportion of at least 50.875% for 1/6-isolated zeta zeros, a proportion above 13/20 for sufficiently small isolation constant, and a 31% lower bound for critical-line zeros of qualifying two-term Dirichlet L-function combinations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The 31% application concerns two distinct primitive Dirichlet characters with the same conductor and parity and nonzero real coefficients; isolation is measured relative to average local zero spacing.
sections.unique_caveat: The 13/20 proportion requires a sufficiently small isolation constant; the 31% statement applies only to the specified character pairs and linear combinations.

sections.title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space
sections.abstract: The author proves a dimension-independent first-order query lower bound matching the known Riemannian-subgradient upper bound in its dependence on curvature and target accuracy.
sections.claimed_result: For 0<ε≤2^-9, the paper establishes worst-case query complexity Θ(ζ_r/ε²), where ζ_r=r/tanh(r), for deterministic first-order methods under its dimension-independent hyperbolic optimization model.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Hyperbolic space of curvature −1; globally geodesically convex, M-Lipschitz functions with a global minimizer in a radius-r ball; exact value-and-subgradient oracle, with dimension allowed to grow with the query horizon.
sections.unique_caveat: The author notes that a concurrent arXiv paper posted about a week earlier obtains the same asymptotic complexity; this work uses a distinct construction for arbitrary deterministic queries.

sections.title: Uniform convergence of canonical discrete uniformization on equilateral approximations
sections.abstract: The authors prove uniform convergence of canonical discrete uniformization maps on increasingly fine equilateral polygonal-disk approximations to the normalized Riemann map, including convergence on the closed reference triangle.
sections.claimed_result: The paper proves Conjecture 7.3 of Luo, Sun, and Wu for the original construction, using compactness, marked lattice limits, estimates at logarithmic cusp scales, an envelope comparison, and a local affine-energy argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sequences of equilateral polygonal disks with mesh tending to zero and marked Jordan boundaries converging uniformly; the limit is the normalized Riemann map.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is stated for this specific equilateral approximation and boundary-convergence setting; broader discretizations are not covered by the abstract.

sections.title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
sections.abstract: The authors resolve a 1991 extremal-graph problem up to polylogarithmic factors for every even minimum-degree target s, and give a related extremal-family result that also covers odd s>3.
sections.claimed_result: For even s≥4 and n-vertex graphs with minimum degree d≥s, every such graph contains a subgraph with minimum degree at least s on O_s(max{n d^{-s/(s-2)}(log n)^180, log n}) vertices; a second theorem gives ex(n,H)=O(n^{2-2/s+ε}) for an appropriate finite family H.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graph extremal setting; the first bound requires even s≥4 and d≥s, while the second applies to all positive integers s and ε>0.
sections.unique_caveat: The first theorem has a polylogarithmic factor with exponent 180 and is stated up to polylogarithmic factors; it covers even s only.

sections.title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk
sections.abstract: The author proves Allaart’s conjecture that the critical probabilities in a semi-best stopping problem for a Bernoulli random walk converge to one half.
sections.claimed_result: For the stated semi-best selection problem, the sequence of critical probabilities p_n tends to 1/2; the limiting stopping and continuation values imply eventual optimality of stopping in the critical state for each fixed p<1/2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bernoulli random walk with up-step probability p and down-step probability 1-p; the stopping time is chosen to maximize the probability of stopping within one unit of the running maximum.
sections.unique_caveat: The result addresses this specific stopping objective and critical state; the abstract gives no convergence rate for p_n.

sections.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression
sections.abstract: For linearly separable data, the authors show that gradient descent can reach any prescribed optimality gap in an iteration count independent of that gap, provided the step size is chosen sufficiently large as a function of target accuracy and data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish an iteration count T independent of ε for attaining ε optimality gap, with T depending on data properties such as sample count and margin, while the required step size depends on ε and another data quantity in dimensions at least three.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Multiclass logistic-regression loss on a linearly separable dataset; sufficiently large target-dependent step size and the paper’s specified data conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: A fixed iteration count does not mean an accuracy-independent step size: η must be selected as a function of ε and dataset properties.

sections.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
sections.abstract: The authors formulate conjectures connecting weight filtrations of Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov motives with quantum-group representation structures and present evidence using a deformation of the representation ring and Hodge-theoretic tools.
sections.claimed_result: The paper proposes relationships between KZ-motive weight filtrations and tilting modules plus the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and gives evidence rather than claiming a complete proof of those conjectures.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: KZ connections associated with finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra at rational parameter, where the resulting local systems admit the stated motivic realizations.
sections.unique_caveat: The central relationships are explicitly conjectural; the abstract reports evidence, not a proved identification of the filtrations.
